summary: EXAMPLE threat-model plan for one repo (payments-api), one Confluence space (ARCH), a design-docs folder and the SEC standards space. The Planner adapts ids, paths and filters to your answers; replace <...> skill sections with your skill's real headings.

questions.question: Which repos/services are in scope, and what is out of scope?
Which Confluence spaces/labels/page trees describe the system? Include attachments?
Where are the internal security standards and processes?
Are CONFLUENCE_URL / CONFLUENCE_TOKEN set in the VS Code terminal environment?

units.title: Inventory payments-api codebase

skill.section: Phase 1 — Gather (all units independent → same wave)

units.instructions: Inventory services/payments-api using text search and targeted reads only: components, entry points, data stores, external calls, authn/authz, secrets, crypto/TLS, IaC/Docker/K8s/CI, dependency manifests. Cite file:line for every item.

units.title: Pull Confluence space ARCH with attachments
units.instructions: Run `python .agents/tools/confluence.py --job kb-conf-ARCH --space ARCH --attachments`; re-run while status is time_slice. Then run the printed convert.py command for attachments, then `python .agents/tools/batch.py --job kb-conf-ARCH --add-units --question "architecture, components, data flows, trust boundaries, data classification, security controls, dependencies"` (and the same batch command for kb-conf-ARCH-att if it has pages).

units.title: Convert design and infrastructure documents
units.instructions: Run `python .agents/tools/convert.py --job kb-docs --inputs docs/hld docs/infra`; re-run while time_slice; then `python .agents/tools/batch.py --job kb-docs --add-units --question "architecture, components, data flows, trust boundaries, data classification, security controls, dependencies"`.

units.title: Build the internal standards catalog
units.instructions: Run `python .agents/tools/confluence.py --job kb-standards --space SEC --label standard`; re-run while time_slice; then `python .agents/tools/batch.py --job kb-standards --add-units --question "list every requirement as: ID | requirement (short) | applies to | how compliance is evidenced"`.

units.title: Turn architecture images into models
units.instructions: For every image in .agents/cache/*/images.json: if the diagram-to-dsl skill is installed, run its parser and save the model and C4/Mermaid output under threat-model/inventory/diagrams/. List images it cannot parse with a one-line reason.

units.title: Build the system model and schedule threat groups
units.instructions: From the inventories, diagrams.md and the summary.md files only, write the system model (components, stores, external entities, Mermaid DFD, trust boundaries, data classification, assets), citing sources and listing doc/code conflicts. Then split it into groups (<=5 elements or one trust boundary) and add per group with ledger.py add: T-<group> (Implementer, depends on M-REVIEW), C-EVID-<group> (Fetcher, depends on T-<group>), C-JUDGE-<group> (Reviewer, depends on C-EVID-<group>), using the playbook's Phase 3-4 instructions and estimates.

units.title: Review the system model
units.instructions: Spot-check 3-5 elements of threat-model/system-model.md against the sources they cite; look for missing trust boundaries and wrong flows. PASS or add fix units.

units.title: Assemble the threat model report
units.instructions: Assemble threat-model/THREAT_MODEL.md in the skill's template from system-model.md, threats/*.md and credibility/*.md: scope, assumptions, model + DFD, threats by residual risk with verdicts, gaps vs standards (std ID -> threat -> recommended control), doc/code conflicts, open questions, sources.

units.title: Final review against the request
units.instructions: Check THREAT_MODEL.md against the original request and the skill's quality bar; every verdict must cite a standard and evidence.
